theme: 3 terms on handing work to another object: the helper, the one that supplies content, and the function it calls

terms.definition: An object that another object hands some of its decisions and events to.
terms.example: Set the view controller as the Delegate, so it hears the taps.

terms.definition: An object that supplies the content a view needs to show, like how many rows and what is in each.
terms.example: The Data Source says there are twenty rows.

terms.definition: A function that the delegate implements, so the other object can call it when something happens.
terms.example: Implement the Delegate Method `didSelectRowAt`, the table calls it on each tap.

quizzes.question: What supplies the rows and the content a table needs to show?
In this code, what is the whole function called?
What do you call an object that another object hands some of its decisions to?

video.title: Delegate, Data Source & Delegate Method | Day 97
video.description:
Learn to explain how UIKit asks your code what to show and what to do: Delegate, Data Source & Delegate Method, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Delegate - An object that another object hands some of its decisions and events to.
Data Source - An object that supplies the content a view needs to show, like how many rows and what is in each.
Delegate Method - A function that the delegate implements, so the other object can call it when something happens.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 97 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.title: iOS Delegate, Data Source & Delegate Method | Day 97
landscape.description:
Explain Delegate, Data Source & Delegate Method in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
델리게이트, 데이터 소스, 델리게이트 메서드 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Delegate - An object that another object hands some of its decisions and events to.
한국어: 델리게이트: 다른 객체가 일부 결정과 이벤트를 대신 맡기는 객체

Data Source - An object that supplies the content a view needs to show, like how many rows and what is in each.
한국어: 데이터 소스: 행이 몇 개인지, 각 행에 무엇이 들어가는지처럼 뷰가 보여 줄 내용을 공급하는 객체

Delegate Method - A function that the delegate implements, so the other object can call it when something happens.
한국어: 델리게이트 메서드: 무언가 일어났을 때 상대 객체가 호출할 수 있도록 델리게이트가 구현하는 함수

In this video, Mina and Jake find out why a table shows no rows, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Your table is empty. Can you explain why in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my table is empty. No rows at all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you set the Data Source?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the bug. The Delegate handles taps. The Data Source supplies the rows through `numberOfRowsInSection`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Delegate is only for events?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mostly, yes. It also answers small questions, like the row height.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. Which Delegate Method runs when I tap a row?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: `didSelectRowAt`. The table calls that Delegate Method for you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And `numberOfRowsInSection` belongs to the Data Source?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Correct. Set both to `self` and your rows appear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Done. Now I see all twenty rows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Delegate. I set it to `self`.
